layers.note: A herb of prairies and rocky balds, half-parasitic on the roots of grasses.

moisture.note: Dry, well-drained prairie soils on glacial outwash.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 2,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Maritime and inland winters both: coldest-month means from about −10 °C (gone by −16 °C), as from the coast to the interior mountains.

hard_freeze_c.note: Cold-hardy: lows to about −34 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −42 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warmest-month means from about 12.5 to 24 °C; gone below 10 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,800 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,100.

degree_days_5.note: About 800 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 400: from the lowlands to the montane forest.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; its range takes in summer-dry coasts and interior mountains with some summer rain, to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Harsh paintbrush grows in prairies and open slopes from British Columbia to Oregon and east to Montana (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
